name: Flucloxacillin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Flucloxacillin is partly excreted in urine (20% to 50% of an oral dose) and is not removed by hemodialysis. The Irish label usually needs no dose reduction in kidney impairment; below creatinine clearance (CrCl) 10 mL/min it advises a lower dose or longer interval, with high-dose regimens capped at 1 g every 8 to 12 hours. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Irish summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); single threshold at 10 mL/min.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 250 to 500 mg orally three times daily; up to 8 g/day in divided doses every 6 to 8 hours for osteomyelitis or endocarditis (SmPC).
No dose reduction usually needed at CrCl ≥10 (SmPC). Watch for neurotoxicity with high intravenous doses.
CrCl 10–14: no change. CrCl <10: reduce the dose or extend the interval; with high-dose regimens give no more than 1 g every 8 to 12 hours (SmPC).
bands.short: CrCl <10: high dose max 1 g q8–12h

hd.text: Dose as for CrCl <10 (high-dose regimens maximum 1 g every 8 to 12 hours). Not significantly removed by hemodialysis; no supplementary dose needed (SmPC).
hd.short: High dose: max 1 g q8–12h; no supplement

pd.text: No PD-specific data; dose as for CrCl <10 (maximum 1 g every 8 to 12 hours for high-dose regimens).

crrt.text: No data in the SmPC. Specialist input.

dialyzable: No: not significantly removed by hemodialysis (SmPC).
monitoring: Liver and kidney function during prolonged courses (cholestatic jaundice, hepatitis). High anion gap metabolic acidosis with paracetamol, especially in severe kidney impairment or sepsis; check urinary 5-oxoproline if suspected. Potassium (hypokalemia at high doses). Sodium load about 51 mg per gram (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: All ages, including newborns with caution (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: Over 10 years: adult dose. 2 to 10 years: half the adult dose. Under 2 years: one-quarter of the adult dose (SmPC).
pediatric.notes: Newborns: caution (hyperbilirubinemia, kernicterus, reduced renal excretion).

renal.recommendation: Normal kidney function: usual age-based doses (SmPC).
No pediatric-specific kidney data; adult rule (no change unless CrCl <10) is a reasonable guide.

No pediatric-specific kidney data; adult rule: reduce dose or extend interval.

adult: Only the capsule SmPC was retrieved; injection SmPC dosing not checked.
The SmPC does not define 'reduce the dose' numerically except the 1 g q8–12h cap for high-dose regimens.
